source.title: Workflow aborts before the first node when safeRegex times out in internal displayOptions validation

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

A production webhook execution aborted before any workflow node ran because the 250 ms `safeRegex` guard timed out while n8n was checking its own node-description `displayOptions`. The pattern/input involved in the identified validation path are a fixed model-name predicate and short configured model IDs, not message text or a user-supplied regex.

The persisted execution error only contained the queue/Bull failure stack. The original useful stack was recovered independently from both the worker and webhook container logs. `startData` and `runData` were empty and `nodeExecutionStack` was empty. Total failed execution duration was 839 ms.

```text
Error: Regular expression execution timed out
  at run (n8n-workflow/src/safe-regex.ts:131:32)
  at Object.test (n8n-workflow/src/safe-regex.ts:149:11)
  at Object.test (n8n-workflow/src/safe-regex.ts:193:42)
  at n8n-workflow/src/node-helpers.ts:397:17
  at checkConditions (n8n-workflow/src/node-helpers.ts:345:20)
  at displayParameter (n8n-workflow/src/node-helpers.ts:450:24)
  at displayParameterPath (n8n-workflow/src/node-helpers.ts:504:9)
  at getParameterIssues (n8n-workflow/src/node-helpers.ts:1528:22)
  at getParameterIssues (n8n-workflow/src/node-helpers.ts:1714:20)
  at Object.getNodeParametersIssues (n8n-workflow/src/node-helpers.ts:1271:20)
  at WorkflowExecute.checkReadyForExecution (n8n-core/src/execution-engine/workflow-execute.ts:897:30)
  at WorkflowExecute.checkForWorkflowIssues (n8n-core/src/execution-engine/workflow-execute.ts:1495:31)
  at WorkflowExecute.processRunExecutionData (n8n-core/src/execution-engine/workflow-execute.ts:1580:8)
  at JobProcessor.processJob (n8n/src/scaling/job-processor.ts:275:34)
```

The installed `safe-regex.js` uses `const REGEX_TIMEOUT_MS = 250` and `script.runInContext(vmContext, { timeout: REGEX_TIMEOUT_MS })`. The module does not read an environment variable for that timeout. The currently fetched master source also retains this constant; we have **not** reproduced a production failure on the latest release and are not claiming that every newer version is affected.

### To Reproduce

**The actual timeout is intermittent. We do not yet have a deterministic trigger for it.** The following probe deterministically identifies the exact internal model-validation path; it normally succeeds and is not itself a deterministic reproduction of the scheduling delay:

1. Use the installed OpenAI Chat Model node v1.2/v1.3, or OpenAI text/message node v1.8, in a webhook workflow.
2. Configure a fixed model ID such as `gpt-5.4` in a resource locator, using either list or ID mode.
3. The `reasoningEffort`/`reasoning_effort` property descriptor has a display condition with `_cnd.regex`:

```js
String.raw`(^o1([-\d]+)?$)|(^o[3-9].*)|(^gpt-5.*)`
```

4. In an isolated process with the installed packages, call `NodeHelpers.getNodeParametersIssues(nodeType.description.properties, node)` and observe `safeRegex.test(pattern, modelId)` invoked from `displayParameter`/`checkConditions`.
5. When the intermittent timeout occurs in this preflight path, the entire execution aborts before node execution, and the persisted error does not identify the node/property/model being checked.

We checked three real node configurations (two chat-model versions and one text/message node). For each, the static configuration calls this regex once. As a temporary workaround, switching the model resource locator to ID mode with an expression returning the **same constant ID** skips that call because `displayParameter` treats expression values as unresolved.

For example: `value: '={{ "gpt-5.4" }}'`. Six isolated baseline/candidate helper checks returned no parameter issues, and n8n's own `Workflow.expression.getSimpleParameterValue` resolved all three candidate IDs and resource locators to their original values. Normalized node options were unchanged. No provider request, workflow replay, or customer message was used for these probes. This verifies the workaround path, **not** the root cause or sustained production effectiveness.

### Expected behavior

Trusted internal node-description checks against short static identifiers should not intermittently abort an otherwise valid workflow before the first node. If a guard must abort, the error should retain the node/property and whether this was internal description validation rather than a user expression.

We are not asking to disable protection for user-authored patterns. Please confirm whether there is an existing tracked fix or supported mitigation specifically for this internal preflight path.

### Debug Info

- Self-hosted Docker Swarm, Linux x64, queue mode with separate editor, webhook and worker.
- n8n: `2.34.6`.
- Node.js in the affected worker: `v24.18.0`.
- Database: PostgreSQL.
- Affected worker limit: 2 CPU and 12 GiB.
- No new OOM/restart or PostgreSQL error was found in the immediate incident window.
- Cumulative cgroup throttling counters exist, but **we have not correlated CPU throttling, steal time or GC with the incident**. CPU pressure is a hypothesis, not a proven diagnosis.
- No complete customer workflow, credentials, payloads, client names or customer identifiers are included in this report.

### Related reports and work

- Similar symptom report: https://community.n8n.io/t/intermittent-regular-expression-execution-timed-out-errors-across-multiple-workflows/310510
- Related draft refactor: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/38490 (splitting user/internal patterns). Its description explicitly states that it does not change default engine behavior; we are not treating it as a confirmed fix for this issue.

### Operating System
Linux x64 (Docker on Ubuntu 24.04)

### n8n Version
2.34.6

### Node.js Version
24.18.0

### Database
PostgreSQL

### Execution mode
queue

### Hosting
self hosted
